intro.caption: Lesson 2-6 — multi-digit division. Clip Squad's merch tour van has to ship 1,248 hoodies in boxes of 24 across three stops. One dropped zero or ignored remainder leaves merch stranded on the curb!

balloons.t: 1,248 hoodies, 24 per box! Figure out the box count before we roll out!
Remember the four steps: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down!

pages.ch: Chapter 1 · Do Not Drop the Zero

balloons.t: I divided 3,672 stickers by 18 and got 24! When 18 didn't fit into 7, I just skipped it!
Skip a digit and you lose a place value! Write 0 in the quotient whenever the divisor does not fit!

pages.caption: Every time you bring down a digit, you must write a digit in the quotient — even when that digit is 0.

balloons.t: Pack the hoodies first, then fix Dex's sticker division without dropping the zero!
1,260 caps divided by 24 gives 52 boxes with 12 caps left over! Do we leave the 12 behind?
Every cap ships! A remainder means we need one more box.
Two highway routes ahead! Check the math on both routes so we don't take a wrong turn.
Multiply the quotient back by the divisor to catch mistakes fast!
Final loading dock! Watch out for zero placeholders and leftover posters!
I am writing every zero this time. Promise!
Every single hoodie, sticker, cap, and poster delivered! Zero merch left behind!

win.caption: Long division repeats divide, multiply, subtract, bring down until no digits remain. Write a 0 in the quotient whenever the divisor does not fit, and round up when a remainder means nothing can be left behind.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Divide with a Zero Hole
gates.prompt: Compute the hoodie boxes (1,248 ÷ 24) and fix Dex's sticker count (3,672 ÷ 18).
hints: Conceptual: every digit you bring down must produce a digit in the quotient, including 0 when the divisor does not fit.
Procedural: repeat divide → multiply → subtract → bring down. Check your answer by multiplying back.

steps: Bring down 9: 24 does not fit into 9, so write 0 in the tens place!
Bring down 6 to make 96: 96 ÷ 24 = 4 (ones). Quotient = 104. Check: 24 × 104 = 2,496.

items.aria: number of hoodie boxes for 1248 divided by 24
items.fbDefault: Divide 124 by 24 (5, with 4 left), bring down 8 to make 48, then divide 48 by 24.

items.aria: number of sticker envelopes for 3672 divided by 18

fb.msg: You dropped the zero! 24 × 18 = 432, way less than 3,672. Write 0 when 18 does not fit into 7.
The 0 goes in the tens place (204), not the ones place (240).

items.fbDefault: 36 ÷ 18 = 2. Bring down 7 (18 fits 0 times, write 0), bring down 2 to make 72, 72 ÷ 18 = 4.

gates.pass: 52 hoodie boxes and 204 sticker envelopes! No dropped zeros on the manifest.

gates.title: Gate 2 · What the Remainder Means
gates.prompt: The squad packs 1,260 caps at 24 per box. Note that 1,260 ÷ 24 = 52 R 12.
hints: Conceptual: the quotient counts full boxes, while the remainder is the leftover items that still need a place.
Procedural: if every item must ship, add 1 extra box to hold the remainder.

steps: Practice: 130 water bottles packed 12 per crate. 130 ÷ 12 = 10 R 10.
10 crates are completely full (120 bottles), with 10 bottles left over.
If all bottles must ship, you need 10 + 1 = 11 crates.
worked.q: If 50 shirts pack 8 per bag (50 ÷ 8 = 6 R 2), how many bags are needed to ship ALL shirts?

items.label: How many FULL boxes of 24 caps are there?
items.aria: number of full boxes of caps

fb.msg: 12 is the remainder (leftover caps), not the number of full boxes.
53 × 24 = 1,272, which is more than 1,260. Only 52 boxes are completely full.

items.fbDefault: Look at the quotient in 1,260 ÷ 24 = 52 R 12.

items.q: Every single cap must ship in a box. How many boxes does the squad need in total?

options.fb: Dropping the remainder leaves 12 caps behind on the sidewalk!

options.t: 53 boxes — the 12 leftover caps need one more box

options.fb: 12 is caps, not boxes. All 12 leftover caps fit in 1 extra box.
You cannot ship a remainder box; round up to 53 whole boxes.

gates.pass: 52 full boxes plus 1 extra box for the 12 leftover caps = 53 boxes total!

gates.title: Gate 3 · Pick the Route
gates.prompt: Verify the math on both branching highway routes before turning.
hints: Conceptual: multiplication undoes division — multiplying quotient × divisor must give back the dividend.
Procedural: watch for zero placeholders in 2,472 ÷ 12, and multiply 21 × 15 to test Dex's claim.

steps: Multiply back: 24 × 10 = 240, which is way below 2,040.
So 24 is wrong — the real quotient is 204.

items.label: Route A · 2,472 ÷ 12 =

fb.msg: You dropped the 0 in the tens place! 26 × 12 = 312, not 2,472.
Check the ones digit: 72 ÷ 12 = 6, so 6 goes in the ones place (206).

items.fbDefault: 24 ÷ 12 = 2, bring down 7 (12 fits 0 times, write 0), bring down 2 to make 72, 72 ÷ 12 = 6.

items.q: Route B computes 3,150 ÷ 15. Dex says the answer is 21. How can Mei prove 21 is wrong without re-dividing?

options.t: Multiply back: 21 × 15 = 315, which is 10 times too small

options.fb: Addition does not check division; multiply the quotient by the divisor.
Multiply 21 × 15 to check whether you land back on 3,150.

gates.pass: Route A = 206, and 21 × 15 = 315 proves 3,150 ÷ 15 is 210, not 21. Smooth driving!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Deliver the Merch
gates.prompt: Unload the final venue order. Watch for zero placeholders and leftover posters!
hints: Conceptual: every brought-down digit needs a quotient digit, and a remainder means one more container when all items must ship.
Procedural: run divide → multiply → subtract → bring down for 4,284 ÷ 14, then interpret 1,000 ÷ 24 = 41 R 16.

steps: Practice: 3,248 ÷ 16. 32 ÷ 16 = 2, bring down 4 (0 times), bring down 8 → 48 ÷ 16 = 3. Answer: 203.
Practice remainder: 250 flyers packed 20 per bundle = 12 R 10. Need 13 bundles to carry all flyers.

items.label: Final stop · 4,284 ÷ 14 =

fb.msg: 360 × 14 = 5,040, too big. Write 0 in the tens place: 306.

items.fbDefault: 42 ÷ 14 = 3, bring down 8 (write 0), bring down 4 to make 84, 84 ÷ 14 = 6.

items.label: 1,000 posters packed 24 per tube (1,000 ÷ 24 = 41 R 16). Tubes needed for ALL posters:
items.aria: number of tubes needed to ship all 1000 posters

fb.msg: 41 tubes only hold 984 posters. The 16 leftover posters need 1 more tube.
Do not add 41 + 16. The 16 posters fit into 1 extra tube.

items.fbDefault: 41 full tubes leave 16 posters out. Add 1 more tube for the remainder.

items.q: Why must you write a 0 in the quotient whenever you bring down a digit and the divisor does not fit?

options.t: To hold that place value so the rest of the digits stay in the right places

options.fb: A 0 in the quotient is a placeholder digit, not the remainder.

options.t: You only write 0 at the very end
options.fb: Write 0 in whichever place the divisor does not fit.

gates.pass: UNLOAD COMPLETE! 306 boxes, 42 poster tubes, and zero dropped placeholders!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-6 — what the tour van taught us
rows: Repeat divide, multiply, subtract, bring down until no digits are left in the dividend.
Every brought-down digit needs a digit above it. If the divisor does not fit, write 0 in the quotient.
When every item must ship, a remainder means you need one more box, tube, or trip.
Multiply quotient × divisor (and add any remainder) to prove you land back on the dividend.
journal.quote: "Skip a zero in the quotient and you leave half the merch on the curb." — Mei
